FAILURES AND ARRANGEMENTS.
[It must not be overlooked that in many cases creditors whose names are published in these lists hold security for their debts, sometimes for the full amount.]

BEACOCK, JOHN WADDINGHAM, late builder, Grimsby.—The adjourned public examination of this debtor took place last week at the Grimsby Bankruptcy Court, but nothing further of importance transpired, and the examination was finally ordered to be closed.

BENNETT, R., late of 11, Park Road, Eastville, lately of 1, Stapleton Place, Horfield, Bristol.—The Receiver for the Bristol district has issued particulars under this failure, from which it appears that the debtor has filed a statement of affairs showing liabilities amounting to £930, and assets nil. The report and observations of the Official Receiver are as follows:—"The debtor, now a builder's foreman, carried on business as a speculative builder at and near Horfield for about seven years previously to the summer of 1895, when he left the country and went to America. He has now returned and has only filed his petition from legal proceedings in connection with which certain committal orders might be obtained against him. The claims of his largest creditors appear to have been satisfied by the conveyance to them of the houses which he had erected at Horfield, the liabilities now scheduled being, with the exception of some loans from friends, of comparatively small amounts. The debtor has filed a detailed deficiency account, but makes the following general statement as to his losses: "In the spring of 1895 I was in difficulties, and several of my creditors pressed me for payment of their accounts. In order to avoid bankruptcy I transferred seventeen houses to seven of the creditors, the loss I amounted to £50 per house (the difference in the selling price and the cost to build). The mortgagees foreclosed on the Horfield properties, preventing my finishing the remaining six houses which I had on hand, and selling them I could, no doubt, have realised at a profit, as I had customers in view." The first meeting of the creditors took place on Thursday last at the offices of the Official Receiver, Bristol, but no resolutions being passed the estate will be wound up in the usual manner.

BOLAND, ALFRED PATRICK JOSEPH, trading as the Greenhill and Joseph, at the Greenhill Estate, Hinds Road, Harrow, residing at 105, Priory Road, Kilburn, builder. The first meeting of the creditors interested under this failure took place on Monday last at the offices of the Official Receiver, Temple Avenue, E.C. The statement of affairs showed gross liabilities amounting to £33,134, and an estimated surplus of £4,698. After the chair man had read over the proofs of debt lodged, it was decided to appoint Mr. Francis Joseph Saffery, chartered accountant, of 14, Old Jewry Chambers, E.C., as trustee, to act in conjunction with a committee of inspection.

CARTER, GEORGE, of 105, Welholme Road, Grimsby, builder and joiner.—The public examination of this debtor took place at the last sitting of the Grimsby Bankruptcy Court, before the Registrar. Replying to questions put by the Official Receiver, the debtor stated that he commenced business about ten years ago. He had also been engaged in building in Hursall, Eastbourne; but that was a blind-maker in Canterbury Road, Kilburn, and he borrowed most of the capital with which he commenced of his brother and other persons. He had also been engaged in building in Hursall, Eastbourne; but that did not prove successful. His principal building was the sum of £450 owing to Mr. Franklyn. He also owed a lot of money to people for the building materials. He afterwards went to Hastings, where he commenced business as a blind-maker. When Mr. Christmas settled with the creditors he believed a deed of assignment was executed. Debtor was questioned as to his whereabouts from July 9th to the 13th, and he stated that he went to London but that he only took 9s. with him. The Official Receiver said he objected to persons after having been adjudicated bankrupt going about spending money. In the course of his examination the debtor seemed to experience difficulty in recollecting the details of his business, and the Deputy Registrar remarked that he did not think the debtor's answers at all satisfactory, but as he did not think any useful purpose would be answered by keeping the examination open, the debtor was allowed to pass.

DIXON, T. O. & W. J., contractors, Lynton.—These bankrupts attended at the Barnstaple County Court on Tuesday for their adjourned public examination. The liabilities are £10 10s. 2d. The bankrupts were contractors for the Wooden Bay Pier, near Lynton. The bankrupts entered into partnership with Mr. Cassal, and their father advanced them money. —T. O. Dixon was first examined concerning an account he had sent to a Mr. Edward Britt which showed a balance in favour of the firm of £948 19s. 3d. He stated, at first, he did not know the object for which it was sent, but being pressed admitted it was for Mr. Britt to see some friends with a view to getting money to complete the pier after the wreck. In this statement the following claims were omitted: Burt, Boulton, & Haywood, £804; Mr. John Dixon, £3,000; Morris Bros., £28; a Harvey, £89; Davis & Ingram, £33; and Waters & Jones, £34. He assumed these had been omitted by an oversight. In his statement he had put down £703 as accruing from the contract, but not a penny had been received. By Mr. Goodchild (for the petitioning creditors, Messrs. Burt, Boulton, & Co.): The pier had since been completed by the father, who was guarantor. Eventually the examination was closed.

FILER, ALBERT, Cheltenham Road, Bristol, and JONES, ROBERT, late of Bedminster, Bristol, formerly trading in copartnership as builders.—The public examination of these bankrupts was appointed to be held on Friday at the Bristol Bankruptcy Court before the Registrar, Mr. Harley, but the debtor Jones did not appear. Replying to questions put by the Official Receiver, the debtor Filer stated that he was first in business by himself and built several houses. The amount due to the fully-secured creditors was £8,113, but more than half the mortgages would be debtor's own. Neither of the partners was restricted from private work, and Jones built several houses at St. George's and Burnham. They worked the Cheltenham Road estate in partnership. He had not the slightest idea as to where Jones was now, as he had not seen him since July 3rd, when he said he should "not stop to go through it." He asked witness to go with him. A month before the petition was filed witness saw difficulties ahead. After debtor had been questioned by Mr. Broad, who appeared on his behalf, the examination was ordered to be adjourned until October.
